seed: Dragging a picture in from the Finder used to leave you holding whatever tool you had, so the obvious next move, nudging the picture into place, drew a shape over it instead. The walk holds the rectangle tool, lets a file go on the canvas, and checks the pointer arrived with the picture picked: the drag that follows should MOVE it, and the tree should still hold one picture rather than a picture with a box on top. Then it drops again and presses undo straight away, which should hand the rectangle tool back, and redo should take the pointer up again. Last it lets a file go on a row in the layers list, which has to hand the pointer over the same way.

steps.note: an empty canvas with the rectangle tool in hand, the way anyone who has just drawn a box is holding it
the drop should have handed the pointer over with the dropped picture picked: two layers, tool select
the drag must MOVE the picture: still two layers, the picture somewhere new, no rectangle drawn over it
a second drop, again with the pointer in hand
undo took the drop back out and handed the rectangle tool back with it
redo put the picture back and took the pointer up again
a file let go on a row in the layers list lands where the line promised and hands the pointer over the same way: one more layer, tool select
a marquee drawn before a drop: region should read a rectangle
the drop cleared the marquee, so the next drag moves the picture rather than the pixels inside the old outline: region should read none
